title: Find the best corner

blocks.text: A bakery plans how many oven hours go to each of two products, under rules written as rows of $`Ax \le b`$, and wants the plan with the highest objective $`c^\top x`$. The region is a polygon, and the best plan can be found at one of its corners.
Write `best_corner(A, b, c, tol=1e-9)` in `corner.py`, for two variables. Try every pair of rows $`i < k`$:

items: If the two rows are parallel ($`|\det| < 10^{-12}`$ for the 2-by-2 matrix of the pair), skip the pair.
Otherwise solve $`a_i^\top x = b_i`$, $`a_k^\top x = b_k`$ with `np.linalg.solve`.
Keep the crossing only if it is feasible: every row has $`a_r^\top x \le b_r + \text{tol}`$.

blocks.text: Return `(value, (x0, x1))` for the kept crossing with the largest $`c^\top x`$, as Python floats. Return `None` if no crossing is kept. You may assume the region has at least one corner and that the objective does not grow without limit on it.

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools

import numpy as np


def best_corner(A: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, c: np.ndarray, tol: float = 1e-9) -> tuple[float, tuple[float, float]] | None:
    """The vertex of {x : A @ x <= b} in two variables that maximizes c @ x, as (value, (x0, x1))."""
    A, b, c = np.asarray(A, dtype=float), np.asarray(b, dtype=float), np.asarray(c, dtype=float)
    best = None
    for i, k in itertools.combinations(range(len(b)), 2):
        pair = A[[i, k]]
        if abs(np.linalg.det(pair)) < 1e-12:
            continue
        point = np.linalg.solve(pair, b[[i, k]])
        if np.any(A @ point > b + tol):
            continue
        value = float(c @ point)
        if best is None or value > best[0]:
            best = (value, (float(point[0]), float(point[1])))
    return best


if __name__ == "__main__":
    A = np.array([[1, 1], [-1, 0], [0, -1]])
    print(best_corner(A, np.array([4, 0, 0]), np.array([1, 2])))

cases.says: the vertex with the highest objective is returned with its value
a crossing of two rows that breaks a third row is never returned, however good its objective
a region with parallel rows, such as a box, still gives its best corner
a vertex that floating point places a hair outside a row is still a vertex

origin.section: A Linear Objective Is Best at an Extreme Point

concepts: in two variables the optimum of a linear objective is found by solving each non-parallel pair of rows, keeping the feasible crossings and taking the best
